title: Open Problem: Complexity of 3-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs
statement_text: Determine the complexity of $3$-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs for $t \geq 8$.
context_text: $P_t$ is the path on $t$ vertices, and $P_t$-free means having no induced subgraph isomorphic to $P_t$. For fixed $k\ge3$, $k$-colourability is NP-complete on $F$-free graphs whenever $F$ contains a cycle or a claw, so the interesting case is when $F$ is a disjoint union of paths. Polynomial-time algorithms for $k$-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs exist for $t\le5$ (all $k$), for $(k,t)=(4,6)$ and for $(k,t)=(3,7)$, while Huang showed $4$-colourability is NP-complete for $P_7$-free graphs and $5$-colourability is NP-complete for $P_6$-free graphs. So $3$-colourability is polynomial for $P_7$-free graphs and open for $t\ge8$. The authors show that, for multigraphs $H$ in which any two distinct vertices have at most one common neighbour, the generating function of (list) homomorphisms from a $P_t$-free graph $G$ to $H$ can be computed in time $2^{O(\sqrt{tn\log n})}$, $n=|V(G)|$; this covers deciding and counting $3$-colourings (homomorphisms to $K_3$) and computing the independent set polynomial, so both problems are solvable in subexponential time on $P_t$-free graphs. The key property is that $P_t$-free graphs have pathwidth $O(t\Delta)$, linear in the maximum degree $\Delta$. In contrast, assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis no subexponential algorithm exists for $4$-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs. The authors remark that this suggests an NP-hardness proof for $3$-colourability of $P_t$-free graphs ($t$ large) via bounded-size gadgets from 3-SAT is unlikely under ETH.

title: Open Problem: Polynomial-time maximum independent set on $P_t$-free graphs
statement_text: Determine whether maximum independent set is decidable in polynomial time for $P_t$-free graphs for $t \geq 7$.
context_text: $P_t$ is the path on $t$ vertices, and $P_t$-free means having no induced subgraph isomorphic to $P_t$. Brause and, independently, Bacsó, Marx and Tuza showed that a greedy exhaustive approach gives a subexponential-time algorithm for maximum independent set on $P_t$-free graphs. The authors show that, for multigraphs $H$ in which any two distinct vertices have at most one common neighbour, the generating function of (list) homomorphisms from a $P_t$-free graph $G$ to $H$ can be computed in time $2^{O(\sqrt{tn\log n})}$, $n=|V(G)|$; this covers deciding and counting $3$-colourings (homomorphisms to $K_3$) and computing the independent set polynomial, so both problems are solvable in subexponential time on $P_t$-free graphs. The key property is that $P_t$-free graphs have pathwidth $O(t\Delta)$, linear in the maximum degree $\Delta$. The authors also ask whether, for fixed $t$, $3$-colourability and maximum independent set are polynomial-time solvable on graphs with no induced cycle of length greater than $t$, since their algorithm extends to that class using Seymour's tree decompositions.
